items.text: The riff that opens Ye Entrancemperium is taken from an unfinished Mayhem song, so Euronymous is credited in the liner notes.
items.why: Background: 'The opening guitar riff to "Ye Entrancemperium" is taken from an unnamed Mayhem song. As such, Mayhem guitarist Euronymous is credited in the album liner notes'; 'this unfinished track'.

Infobox 'Released: May 19, 1997' and Lead 'released on 19 May 1997'. But the pack conflicts with itself: Release section says 'released on 8 July 1997 through Candlelight Records' and Wikidata gives 1997-01-01. Needs a human check before shipping.

items.text: October to December 1996, Grieg Hall, Bergen, Norway
items.why: Infobox: 'Recorded: October–December 1996', 'Studio: Grieg Hall ( Bergen , Norway )'.
Infobox: 'Producer: Eirik Hundvin , Ihsahn and Samoth'.

items.text: Compared with In the Nightside Eclipse, the lyrics shifted away from nature and Satanic themes toward mystical ones.
items.why: Release: 'the album's lyrical themes began to move away from nature and Satanic elements and began to incorporate more mystical themes'. Pack says 'began to move away' and 'more mystical'; the note sharpens it into a completed shift. The comparison with In the Nightside Eclipse is stated in the pack for the music, not the lyrics, though it is implied.

items.text: In 1996 the Reverence EP came out to tease this record, and it included the track The Loss and Curse of Reverence.
items.why: Release: 'In 1996, the EP Reverence, which included the track "The Loss and Curse of Reverence", was released as a teaser for the album'.

items.text: Because the riff comes from an unnamed Mayhem song, Euronymous, the Mayhem guitarist, gets a credit in the liner notes, even though he had died three years before this record was made.
items.why: Background: 'Euronymous is credited in the album liner notes, even though he was murdered three years before the album was written and recorded'. Repeats the hook almost word for word.

items.text: The Mayhem bootleg Ha Elm Zalag holds a recording of that unfinished track.
items.why: Background: 'A recording of this unfinished track can be found on the Mayhem bootleg Ha Elm Zalag'.

items.text: The album was recorded from October to December 1996 at Grieg Hall in Bergen, Norway.
items.why: Infobox 'October–December 1996'; Background 'recorded in the Grieg Hall in Bergen, Norway'. Repeats the facts table.

items.text: Eirik Hundvin, Ihsahn and Samoth are credited as producers, and Pytten handled engineering and production.
items.why: Infobox producers; Additional personnel: 'Pytten – engineering and production'.

items.text: Ihsahn sang and played guitar and synthesizer, and he and Samoth both have arrangement credits.
items.why: Emperor: 'Ihsahn – vocals, guitar; synthesizer, arrangement ...; Samoth – guitar, arrangement ...'.

items.text: Samoth played guitar, Alver played bass, and Trym played drums and percussion.
items.why: Emperor: 'Samoth – guitar ...; Alver – bass; Trym – drums and percussion'.

items.text: The playing is faster and more guitar-driven than on the band's previous album, with fewer keyboards, more clean singing and more blast-beat drumming.
items.why: Release: 'In contrast to the band's previous album ... Anthems showcases a faster, more guitar-driven performance with less usage of keyboards and more clean singing and blast-beat style drumwork'.

items.text: In 1998 the record was remastered and reissued along with three tracks from the Reverence EP that were not on the album.
items.why: Release: 'In 1998, the album was remastered and re-released with the three non-album tracks from Reverence'.

items.text: The band also made a promotional video for The Loss and Curse of Reverence, a track that appears on the EP and on the album.
items.why: Release: 'The band made a promotional video for "The Loss and Curse of Reverence"'; it is track 5 in the Track listing and on the EP.

items.text: The opening guitar riff comes from an unnamed Mayhem song, and a recording of that unfinished track is on the bootleg Ha Elm Zalag.
items.why: Background, as above. Title matches. Third telling of the same fact (hook, section, listen_for).

items.where: listen_for: The Loss and Curse of Reverence
items.text: It is also on the 1996 Reverence EP, the teaser for the album, and a promotional video was made for it.
items.why: Release: EP Reverence 1996 'released as a teaser for the album'; 'promotional video'. Title matches. Repeats two section sentences.

items.text: It is an orchestral version of Inno a Satana, a different take on that song.
items.why: Track listing: '10. "Opus a Satana" (orchestral version of " Inno a Satana ")'. Title matches. 'a different take on that song' adds nothing. The pack lists it as track 10, after the eight-track run, so it may be a reissue bonus; the note does not say so.

missed: The sound itself: Huey's points on crisper, clearer production that lets the arrangements' details come through, more classical flourishes and audible guitar interplay between Ihsahn and Samoth, and the back-cover line 'Emperor performs Sophisticated Black Metal Art exclusively'; also the Finnish chart peak at number 28. Space for these was spent telling the Mayhem riff story three times.
